review_notes: Read the whole file and Mathlib's `coker`/`coker.π` definitions. I also searched the formal-frontier libraries for the same pattern and found one similar use in finite-group-tate-cohomology/Basic.lean, around line 213. The `hom_app` and `inv_app` proofs are the same argument with `.hom` replaced by `.inv`. I did not look for further repetition in `tensorNormalizedChainCokerNatIso_app`, which uses a different argument. I could not compile anything. I am confident that the proposed generic lemma holds mathematically, but I have not checked that its statement elaborates or that the `rfl`/`change` step goes through. findings.problem: The two theorems have the same proof. Each takes `(coker.π _).naturality` at the component of `mapArrowFunctor.map α` at `Arrow.mk f` (once with `α = hom`, once with `α = inv`), applies `.symm`, and then uses a long `change ... at h` to normalize the arrow endpoints before `exact h`. The only difference is `.hom` versus `.inv` and the swapped source and target. The long `change` type ascriptions are written out twice, so any change to the cokernel iso or to the endpoint normalization has to be made in two places. The facts being proved are really about a general natural transformation, not specifically about `tensorNormalizedChainNatIso`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one generic lemma before the two theorems, for functors `F G : SSet.{w} ⥤ ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max a w p} ℤ) ℕ` and `α : F ⟶ G`. Its statement is `cokernel.π (F.map f) ≫ (Functor.whiskerRight ((Functor.mapArrowFunctor SSet.{w} _).map α) (coker _)).app (Arrow.mk f) = α.app T ≫ cokernel.π (G.map f)`. The proof is the existing one: `.symm` of `(coker.π _).naturality (((mapArrowFunctor _ _).map α).app (Arrow.mk f))`, followed by one `change`/`exact`. The `.hom` and `.inv` theorems would then be `exact` applications of this lemma to `(tensorNormalizedChainNatIso A).hom` and `.inv`. This assumes the `.hom.app`/`.inv.app` of `isoWhiskerRight` unfold definitionally to `whiskerRight` applied to `mapArrowFunctor.map hom`/`inv`, with `Functor.map_comp` and `mapIso` unfolding. I have not compiled that. If the unfolding does not go through, a `Functor.isoWhiskerRight_hom` or `isoWhiskerRight_inv` rewrite should do it. Each rewritten theorem becomes a one- or two-line call, and the single `change` in the lemma is stated with generic `F` and `G` and no tensor-specific names.
findings.benefit: The arrow-endpoint normalization is written once instead of twice, and the two theorems shrink to one-line applications. The `hom` and `inv` statements are visibly the same fact. The generic lemma is not tied to the tensor-chain setting, so a later nat-iso built the same way can reuse it. This follows the existing `Functor.isoWhiskerRight` / `coker.π` pattern without duplicating the proof.
